chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn al-Walid and Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Yunus ibn Yaqub, from Ali ibn Isa al-Qammat, from his uncle, from Abu Abdullah ibn Abi Ya'fur (his uncle), from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) saw in his dream the Clan of Umayya ascending upon his pulpit after him, and straying the people from the Path back on their heels, so he became bleak and sad.

So Jibraeel (peace be upon him) descended unto him and said: 'O Messenger of Allah! Why do I see you as bleak and sad?' He said: 'O Jibraeel! I saw the Clan of Umayya in my night ascending my pulpit after me, and straying the people from the Path back on their heels.'

He said: 'By the One who sent you with the Truth as a Prophet! This is something I have not been notified of.' So he ascended to the sky, and it was not long before he descended unto him with a Verse from the Quran to comfort him with it.
Have you then considered if We were to let them enjoy themselves for years, then comes to them that with which they are threatened, that which they were made to enjoy shall not avail them?

And there was Revealed unto him: 'Surely We revealed it in the Night of Predestination, and what will make you realize what the Night of Predestination is? The Night of Predestination is better than a thousand months.'
Allah, Mighty and Majestic, made the Night of Pre-determination for His Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) to be better than a thousand months of the kingdom of the Clan of Umayya.

key_terms.الصِّرَاطِ الْقَهْقَرَى: The Path back on their heels (straying)

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of Laylat al-Qadr in relation to the rule of the Clan of Umayya according to this hadith?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) experiences sorrow upon dreaming of the Banu Umayya usurping the pulpit and leading the community astray. Jibraeel (peace be upon him) ascends to heaven and returns with verses from Surah Al-Qadr, specifically highlighting that the Night of Decree is 'better than a thousand months.' Shia scholars interpret this as a divine compensation where the spiritual merit of Laylat al-Qadr outweighs the entire duration of Umayyad political rule, offering solace for their temporal dominance.
